The retail and apartment buildings were demolished as part of the "Renaissance Project” that were a key element in revitalizing downtown Newport in 2015. title: INTC, AMD, NVDA, MU: Chip Stocks Open Mixed Premarket After Worst Week In A Month - Stocktwits
content: U.S. semiconductor stocks opened mixed in Monday’s premarket session after a bruising week for the sector, as concerns over OpenAI’s revenue outlook and intensifying competition in the memory-chip market weighed on investor sentiment. Nvidia (NVDA) shares were up 0.1%. Intel (INTC) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stocks fell 1% and 0.6%, respectively, dragging the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) down 1.5%. Broadcom (AVGO) shed 0.3%. SOXX fell about 5% over the past week, its worst weekly performance in a month, reflecting mounting pressure on chipmakers amid questions about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. DRAM declined 7.4% in the week, its worst run in nearly three months. Micron faced pressure on Monday after Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced progress in advanced DRAM technology. The development has raised concerns about growing competition in a market dominated by established players such as Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. The move comes as U.S. semiconductor stocks face renewed pressure following a strong rally this year, with investors booking profits and reassessing the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Last week, chip stocks tumbled after reports said OpenAI’s annualized revenue was around $50 billion at the end of September, below the $68 billion to $70 billion figures previously circulated in the market. The discrepancy raised concerns about whether the AI startup’s revenue growth could justify the enormous investments in AI infrastructure, including data centers and advanced processors. Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and Micron were among the chipmakers caught in the selloff. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment was ‘bullish’ for MU and DRAM, ‘bearish’ for NVDA, SOXX and ‘neutral’ for AMD as of early Monday. With semiconductor stocks facing pressure from multiple directions, investors will be watching for signs of stabilization as the third-quarter earnings season gathers pace. Results from ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) this week would be catalysts for the broader sector. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. U.S. stock futures were higher early Monday as investors geared up for the official start of the third-quarter earnings season, with major U.S. banks reporting and tech reports from ASML and TSMC this week. As of 4:00 a.m. ET, Nasdaq, S&P 500, Dow and Russell 2000 futures gained 0.2%. The modest gains followed a strong week on Wall Street, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq hitting record highs. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 Index, and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, has moved to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ last week. Oil prices dipped after President Donald Trump declared an immediate “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, though crude remained above $100 a barrel amid escalating Middle East tensions following a Houthi strike on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend. U.S. Treasury markets are closed on Monday for Columbus Day, even as U.S. stock markets remain open. The Q3 reporting period begins this week with major financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS), Citigroup (C) and Wells Fargo (WFC) reporting on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America (BAC), Morgan Stanley (MS) and other major financial companies on Wednesday. Meanwhile, September’s Consumer Price Index is due on Wednesday, followed by Producer Price Index data and retail sales on  Thursday. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled to speak on Thursday at the 2026 Annual Meetings of the Boards of Governors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group. Micron Technology (MU), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSM): Shares dipped 1% in early premarket trade as China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) reportedly advanced work on next-generation DRAM technology. TSM will also report earnings later this week, with investors watching for commentary on AI demand. Separately, Elon Musk’s plans for Terafab, a proposed chipmaking initiative tied to Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX), have brought the semiconductor supply chain back into focus. Reports indicate TSMC is considering a role in the Texas project, and Intel is also advancing its involvement. Over the weekend, Musk unveiled plans for Terafab, aiming to iterate rapidly on 10 internal chip designs per year. Apple (AAPL) is on the watchlist ahead of developments around its smart-home strategy. Iren (IREN): Shares rose 5% in early premarket trade following reports that Anthropic signed a multiyear data center cloud deal with the company. Amazon (AMZN): Shares inch higher in early premarket trading after reports indicate the company is in talks to acquire AI startup Decart for around $7 billion to enhance its use of custom Trainium chips. Palantir Technologies (PLTR): Hovering near record highs as retail bulls embrace recent Wall Street upgrades despite its CTO dismissing reports regarding software usage in foreign strikes. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): Shares trending higher in early premarket following news that its BlueBird 14–16 satellites arrived at Cape Canaveral for launch, alongside FCC clearance for 900-MHz testing. Rocket Lab (RKLB): NASA’s chief has reportedly warned that the lunar race with China is very ‘close’, with analysts highlighting expanding commercial opportunities for its Neutron rocket. Chinese Electric Vehicle Makers (NIO, BYD, XPEV): Watching EU regulatory updates as reports suggest a 350,000-vehicle annual cap on Chinese hybrid imports starting December 1. XPEV is also on the retail radar after executives said its advanced driver-assistance software can adapt to European roads with minimal additional AI training data. Sellas Life Sciences (SLS): Shares rose in early premarket trade after retail traders speculated that a massive booth reserved for the upcoming ASH conference points toward potential M&A or partnership talks. Fannie Mae (FNMA), Freddie Mac (FMCC): In his latest Substack note, Michael Burry revealed that he has swapped common shares for preferred stock to manage dilution risks. SoFi Technologies (SOFI): Shares remained in focus after Keefe, Bruyette & Woods lowered its price target to $15 from $16 and maintained an Underperform rating. WF Holding (WFF): Pulling back after a massive speculative rally of over 450% on Friday. Other tickers trending on Stocktwits at the time of writing included Boost Run (BRUN), Rivian (RIVN), Starbucks (SBUX), and Chipotle (CMG). On the economic front, traders will tune in for Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack’s speech today at 12:10 pm ET, ahead of key inflation data (September CPI on Wednesday and PPI on Thursday) and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s speech later in the week. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Delta Air Lines Inc. (DAL) stock edged higher overnight as CEO Ed Bastian revisited the airline’s past discussions with Elon Musk’s Starlink amid tensions between the two sides. Bastian said Delta tested Starlink’s technology years ago, but disagreements over deployment timelines and customer access prevented a deal, while stressing he remains a fan of the satellite internet service. Delta Air Lines stock edged 0.04% higher in Monday’s premarket. The stock dropped 2.2% last week. In a CNBC interview on Friday, Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian said the airline explored a partnership with SpaceX’s (SPCX) Starlink internet service years ago. “We've been around Starlink for a lot of years. In fact, we had conversations 6 years ago when Starlink was just launching. We in fact gave them some of our planes to test it out, and it was fabulous." "They just weren't ready to scale when we were ready to go. We had disagreements on the business model in terms of access to the customer. I'm a big fan of Starlink." Bastian added that Delta was among the first to make free, high-speed Wi-Fi a standard service. Delta is working closely with Viasat and Hughes to improve onboard connectivity. “Delta is the global pioneer in launching free and fast WiFi as the industry standard. We are working very closely with our partners Viasat and Hughes. We have big improvements coming. Just yesterday Viasat got approval from FCC to launch for the U.S. carriers. By the end of this year our customers are going to see meaningful improvements and are excited about Amazon Leo.” Elon Musk’s dispute with Delta Air Lines has grown after the airline declined to use SpaceX’s Starlink Wi-Fi. Musk criticized Delta’s internet service and warned it could “lose customers”. In a company event, Bastian had responded to Musk’s jibe, saying, "We do not want to be with Elon Musk. Trust me." Delta has chosen Amazon Leo for its in-flight Wi-Fi instead. Delta’s stock fell 1% on Friday after the airline reported third-quarter (Q3) results that missed analysts’ expectations. The company posted adjusted earnings of $1.72 per share and revenue of $17.59 billion, below estimates of $1.76 per share and $18.92 billion, according to Fiscal.ai data. Delta also lowered its 2026 earnings forecast as fuel costs kept rising. Delta’s fuel expenses jumped 62% year-on-year to $4.14 billion in the quarter. The airline now expects adjusted earnings of $5.10 - $5.60 per share for 2026, down from its earlier forecast of $6.50 - $7.50. Delta still expects about $2.5 billion in free cash flow for the full year and plans to repay more than $2 billion in debt. “It was a challenging quarter because of the extreme volatility that we saw in fuel prices. But I’ve got to give my thanks and kudos to my team to cover a 60% increase on a year-over-year in fuel prices, which was $ 1.6 billion for us, and not missing our overall profit year-on-year.” On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’ A user said, “Delta Air Lines is one of the clearest plays on the screener theme, with a large global passenger and cargo network whose profitability shifts with jet fuel costs, so any relief in energy prices can quickly change how investors view its earnings power.” Also see: CMG Stock Ticks Higher Overnight: Chipotle’s Digital Strategy Could Support Growth Despite Margin Squeeze, Says Analyst For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Rocket Lab (RKLB) shares rose 0.4% overnight heading into Monday after NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman warned that the U.S. and China are separated by “months, not years” in the race to return astronauts to the moon, shifting investor attention to launch providers. RKLB shares fell 8% to $68.21 last week, marking their worst weekly performance since late August. China aims to land astronauts on the moon by 2029, while NASA is targeting a crewed return by the end of 2028, Isaacman said in a Fox Business interview. “That’s a difference of months, not years,” he said. “This is going to be extremely close right now.” Isaacman said China and Russia are working together on plans for a lunar base and a nuclear power plant near the moon’s south pole. NASA plans to launch its first moon-base mission in December aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy. “The race is very much on,” he said. He also named Rocket Lab as one of the commercial space companies NASA can draw on, alongside SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, and others. The agency is also considering bulk purchases of rocket launches for its estimated $30 billion moon-base effort. Moon Base Program Manager Carlos Garcia-Galan said that NASA is evaluating groups of launch vehicles to serve the program’s needs and expects to announce an initial set of purchases soon. The procurement push comes as demand for launches rises and SpaceX limits new dedicated Falcon 9 bookings beyond 2028 while prioritizing Starship. ARK analysts Tasha Keeney and Daniel Maguire said satellite operators urgently need launch access as they expand their constellations. Keeney said Rocket Lab’s Neutron “comes close to the Falcon 9” in payload capacity. ARK put Neutron’s planned capacity at 13,000 kilograms to low Earth orbit, compared with about 17,000 kilograms for Falcon 9 in a partially reusable configuration. SpaceX’s growing internal launch needs could intensify the squeeze. ARK pointed to Starlink’s planned deployments and upcoming StarMind AI satellites as potential demands on launch capacity, arguing that providers such as Rocket Lab could benefit if Neutron delivers. Rocket Lab is targeting delivery of Neutron to the launch pad in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company has begun building a customer pipeline for the rocket. Kepler Communications booked a dedicated Neutron mission no earlier than 2028, giving it more control over launch timing and orbital placement than a rideshare mission. Rocket Lab is also expanding its Electron business. A 20-launch agreement with Japan’s Synspective brings the customer’s total contracted Electron missions to 47, with launches scheduled between 2028 and 2031. Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) stock ticked higher overnight as investors weighed near-term margin pressures against the chain’s growth plans. Morningstar analyst Ari Felhandler sees potential for recovery, pointing to increased spending on menu innovation, marketing, digital ordering and restaurant technology to attract budget-conscious diners, improve efficiency and support market-share gains. Chipotle Mexican Grill stock gained 0.06% overnight, ahead of Monday. The stock declined 2.4% last week. Morningstar analyst Ari Felhandler believes the burrito chain’s strong brand, digital capabilities and attractive restaurant economics could support further market-share gains despite near-term pressure on sales and profit. Chipotle plans to strengthen its appeal through new menu items, improved service and greater convenience rather than relying heavily on discounts. Felhandler said U.S. systemwide sales increased at a 15% annual rate over the past five years, exceeding the broader foodservice market’s 9% growth and the 10.5% rate for Latin American limited-service restaurants. Morningstar expects the company to invest approximately $4 billion in capital expenditures over the next five years, compared with $2.7 billion during the previous comparable period. Chipotle is introducing additional limited-time menu offerings while upgrading kitchen equipment to improve food preparation speed and consistency. Tools such as automated produce slicers and dual-sided cooking equipment could help restaurants serve more customers efficiently, said the analyst. Chipotle also plans to expand its use of artificial intelligence and automation over time. Felhandler said Chipotle’s digital business could help drive future growth. Its loyalty program has about 21 million active members, and digital orders made up 37% of sales in 2025, up from 18% in 2019. Chipotlanes, which let customers pick up online orders through dedicated drive-thrus, now make up about 30% of its restaurants, making ordering more convenient. Morningstar said Chipotle restaurants generate about $3.1 million in annual sales on average, more than many competitors. The company can recover the cost of opening a new restaurant in about two years, compared with four to six years for many larger chains. This could help Chipotle open more locations in suburban and rural areas across the U.S. and Canada. However, Morningstar expects annual restaurant-unit growth to average 7.3% over the next decade, below management’s target of 8% to 10%. Felhandler kept Morningstar’s fair value estimate for Chipotle at $36 per share. The firm expects operating margins to fall to 14.4% in 2026 before improving in the coming years. Higher wages, rising beef prices, increased advertising and limited price hikes could hurt profits. Still, Morningstar sees Chipotle’s strong brand and restaurant profitability as lasting competitive advantages. On Oct.8, the analyst had opined that a possible acquisition of Chipotle by Starbucks (SBUX) could create a larger restaurant powerhouse, but the added complexity may undermine efforts to strengthen Starbucks’ business after reports of the coffee giant exploring an acquisition of Chipotle Mexican Grill emerged. Morningstar estimates Chipotle could command a valuation of $45 billion to $51 billion, based on 20 to 23 times its EBITDA. At the same time, CEO Elon Musk recalled how short sellers once had the company “in checkmate” during the 2018 Model 3 crisis. TSLA stock jumped 3% last week to $382.70, its best week since late August. “Two years since the 10/10 Cybercab WeRobot event, the cabs are everywhere in Austin now. Dallas soon,” Tesla AI software chief Ashok Elluswamy said on X on Saturday. He was responding to a post from Tesla’s Robotaxi account saying more than 300 Cybercabs were serving Austin, an 8x increase in 30 days. The Dallas hint came after a sharp jump in Tesla’s registered Cybercab fleet. Investor and influencer Sawyer Merritt said on X last week that Texas Department of Motor Vehicles records showed 150 additional registrations, taking the total to 319 from 169. “Tesla just nearly doubled its registered Cybercabs overnight,” he said. It was the largest single-day increase since Cybercabs first appeared in the registry on Aug.31. Austin is the only public Cybercab market, and Tesla has not announced a Dallas launch date. The fleet expansion comes as Tesla prepares to answer federal questions about the Cybercab’s safety certification. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) granted the company a 30-day extension, setting an Oct. 30 deadline rather than the Nov. 20 date Tesla requested. The agency is seeking sworn responses to 21 requests, including how the pedal-free vehicle complies with a braking standard that requires a foot control. Musk addressed the pace of Tesla’s robotaxi expansion in an interview, saying it may look slow even as the fleet grows quickly month to month. “The reason we’re moving what seems to be slowly, although it’s actually a very high percentage increase month over month, is that we want to make sure that we do not have an accident,” he said. “We don’t want to cause an injury or death,” Musk added. “One such thing with a Tesla robotaxi will be worldwide headline news.” He said Tesla reviews difficult road situations before entering a new city. “Before we go to a new city, we want to make sure that there’s not some intersection that’s problematic or risky,” he said. “We want to be particularly careful with railroad crossings.” Musk also spoke about the challenge of detecting small animals in poor visibility. “We have these challenges of literally kittens at night, gray kittens on gray tarmac with tar seams at night in low visibility, and it’s like, ‘Can we not run over the kittens?’” he said. “We actually did solve that, by the way.” He said Tesla tests changes before deploying them and wants to either geofence difficult situations or ensure the system can handle them. Meanwhile, Musk’s short-seller recollection concerned Tesla’s 2018 Model 3 production crisis. “We had to get to 5,000 a week of the Model 3 or go bankrupt,” he said. “The short sellers were actually right,” Musk said of the pressure Tesla faced. “They had us in checkmate.” He recalled that Tesla built a third assembly line in a tent at its Fremont factory, using discarded equipment to move cars down the line. “We were able to increase production by 30% in three weeks,” he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for TSLA slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ levels a day ago amid ‘normal’ message volume. One user said, “$TSLA the strategy/logistics/engineering/etc.  for Cybercab scaling works...Tesla Team Cybercab is  likely implementing ahead of schedule” Tesla says 300+ Cybercabs now serve Austin, and Tesla's Ashok Elluswamy says Dallas is next. Elon Musk's robotaxi push is accelerating. Another user said, “$TSLA full self driving is still not here.  It is the end of 2026.   People still believe.Lol.” So far this year, Tesla's stock has lagged its "Magnificent Seven" peers, making it the group's worst performer, down about 15%. Nvidia's (NASDAQ: NVDA) rapid ascent to the world's most valuable enterprise might be unlike anything the market has ever seen. In the past five years, its share price has produced an incredible 899% gain (as of Oct. 15). With that return, a $10,000 investment would be worth $100,000 today. The driver of this has been, unsurprisingly, artificial intelligence (AI). Nvidia's graphics processing units are the leading chips for training and running AI models. And these hardware devices are a hot commodity among the company's customers. Nvidia's data center revenue soared 117% year over year to $89 billion last fiscal quarter (Q2 2027 ended July 26). Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » A burgeoning industry position in the middle of a generational technology shift is an easy sell to investors right now. History says this AI stock tends to perform well in November, so maybe now is a good time to buy shares. But there's one thing that could break that pattern of positive returns. This decade, Nvidia has been a compelling portfolio addition in November. In November 2020, shares were up 7%. In November 2021 and 2022, they jumped more than 25%. November 2023 saw a 15% increase, followed by a more muted 4% gain in November 2024. The bears finally cheered last year. During the 11th month of 2025, Nvidia stock dipped 13%. Nvidia optimists will take the average return of 13% and conclude that the share price will rise by that much this November. On the other hand, the naysayers will point to the clear deterioration in the stock's monthly performance in recent years. They'll assume shares are set to fall in November. Investors shouldn't jump to any conclusions, however. The macroeconomic backdrop, as well as industry conditions, seem to have been anything but stable. Then there's market sentiment, which is constantly shifting based on how the investment community is feeling at any particular moment. November could bring anything. Let's still assume that there's a higher probability that Nvidia posts a positive return compared to a loss in November. Instead of taking a victory lap, consider what could break that pattern of upbeat results. In my view, it comes down to one thing. Nvidia's most important customer cohort contains the five big hyperscalers. Combined, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta Platforms, and Oracle, as well as other hyperscalers, contributed $49 billion to data center segment sales, which as mentioned, totaled $89 billion in the most recent fiscal quarter. These customers are spending tremendous sums of capital to build AI-related technical infrastructure. The amount of money they allocate to Nvidia products and services depends on how much momentum their businesses have. Specifically, we've seen cloud revenue accelerate for Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in recent quarters. Hyperscaler backlogs have exploded, measured cumulatively at more than $2 trillion. That's an immediate demand signal that helps to alleviate investor concerns about Nvidia's own business strength. Four of the top five hyperscalers will report their third-quarter financial results in the next two weeks. Investors should continue to pay close attention to numbers and commentary related to how their cloud segments perform. The logic is straightforward. Slower cloud growth gives hyperscalers less reason to keep expanding capital expenditures (capex) at the current pace. And any cuts to forecast capex will negatively impact Nvidia's data center business. Furthermore, market sentiment might plummet. If the growth decelerates in Q3, it's not exactly a reason to panic. That doesn't automatically start a trend. And the view is that AI is still in the early innings. However, a slowdown could drive fears that the AI boom is starting to cool. That could pressure Nvidia shares. The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Nvidia wasn't one of them. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. First Solar Inc. (FSLR) stock slipped overnight after Morningstar slashed its fair value estimate, warning that expiring U.S. solar tax credits and fierce competition could squeeze profits even as surging AI data center power demand creates a new growth opportunity. First Solar stock edged 0.7% lower overnight, ahead of Tuesday, after a 1% climb in the regular session. Morningstar analyst Bischof lowered his fair value estimate for the solar panel maker to $191 per share from $206, saying the stock was trading close to its estimated worth as of Monday. The firm maintained its no-economic-moat assessment and ‘Very High Uncertainty’ Rating for First Solar. The analyst believes intense competition and pressure on manufacturing costs prevent the company from building a lasting competitive advantage. The revised valuation reflects weaker expectations for solar panel sales after tax incentives begin expiring in the early 2030s. However, Bischof said First Solar could benefit from growing electricity needs associated with artificial intelligence, data centers and advanced manufacturing. Unlike most solar companies that use silicon, First Solar makes panels with a thin-film material called cadmium telluride. Its manufacturing process reduces dependence on Chinese suppliers, and its panels can perform better in hot and humid weather. The company is also the largest solar module manufacturer headquartered in the Western Hemisphere. Its strong position in the U.S. utility-scale market, where Morningstar estimates it has historically held about 30% market share, gives it an edge as domestic manufacturing policies favor local production. Still, the firm cautions that First Solar's manufacturing costs per watt remain somewhat higher than those of silicon-based competitors. The broader industry has become price-driven as manufacturing capacity expands and technological differences become less durable. First Solar’s pending orders fell to 45.1 gigawatts in June from 50.1 gigawatts at the end of 2025, as it delivered more panels than it secured in new deals. However, existing orders still give investors an idea of the company’s future sales. Morningstar expects First Solar to increase its production capacity to 22 gigawatts by the end of 2027, with investments in the U.S. and India. The firm also expects panel prices to rise slightly in the next few years before falling as tax benefits are reduced. The firm's valuation includes U.S. production credits worth $0.17 per watt. These incentives remain important to profit, making future policy decisions a major risk for investors. First Solar held approximately $1.7 billion in cash and investments at the end of June. Bischof views the company's conservative spending approach and early investment in U.S. manufacturing positively. However, Morningstar warns that the company's dependence on U.S. policy, concentrated sales markets, and an uncertain overseas manufacturing outlook could lead to widely varying financial results. While rising power demand could drive growth, the analyst believes the current share price already reflects First Solar's estimated value. (V) said on Tuesday it received approval from China’s central bank to begin preparing to set up a domestic bankcard clearing institution. This brings the U.S. payments network a step closer to entering China’s domestic payments market. V shares were up more than 1% in the overnight session at the time of writing. Visa said the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) approved its application to begin formal preparations for domestic operations. A local clearing institution would let the company settle domestic yuan transactions directly through its own network. Ryan McInerney, Chief Executive Officer of Visa, described the approval as a “significant step forward” in the company’s commitment to China.He also acknowledged the role of U.S. and Chinese leaders in “pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies.” Visa first applied to establish a bankcard clearing institution in China in May 2020. Since then, the company has worked with Chinese banks on dual-branded cards, with China’s UnionPay handling domestic transactions and Visa processing overseas payments. In January, Visa said cards issued in mainland China could be linked to Apple Pay for overseas use. The approval follows diplomatic engagement between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump raised Visa’s request for access to China’s domestic market during his Beijing visit in May. In September, China’s Ministry of Commerce said it would review and approve applications from foreign financial institutions, including U.S.-funded firms, seeking to operate or set up branches in the country. McInerney joined Trump’s business delegation to Beijing in May and became chair of the US-China Business Council in June. Visa’s rivals have already made progress in China’s domestic payments market. Mastercard’s (MA) Chinese joint venture began processing payments in 2024 after receiving approval in February 2020 to prepare for bankcard clearing operations. American Express (AXP) was the first of the three to receive a processing license in June 2020, after the PBOC approved it in 2018. Shares of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) slipped 0.6% overnight heading into Tuesday as Raymond James called fears of a near-term Starlink challenge to T-Mobile “overblown,” while Morningstar said Verizon’s network gives established carriers a significant edge. SPCX stock closed Monday at $163.42, up 0.5%, after gaining 2% last week for a second straight weekly gain. “We believe the recent fears over competition from SpaceX are overblown, as they are 3+ years away from becoming reality, and competition from larger players is nothing new to T-Mobile,” Raymond James said. The firm raised its rating on T-Mobile to 'Outperform' from 'Market Perform' and set a $170 price target, implying a 12% upside from current levels. SpaceX agreed last week to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800-megahertz spectrum portfolio, which includes up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum. Grain had acquired the licenses from T-Mobile earlier in 2026. The transaction has been reported at around $8 billion. Meanwhile, Morningstar said SpaceX’s spectrum deal raises uncertainty for wireless carriers, but its base case remains that Starlink will not threaten their wireless operations. It raised its uncertainty ratings for Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T to 'High' from 'Medium' and said SpaceX still needs more spectrum and thousands of sites to build a competitive ground network. Morningstar noted that Verizon has the weakest low-band spectrum position among the three major carriers, but still holds more than three times the low-band spectrum depth in most areas. Building a large terrestrial network could be a poor use of capital in a mature market, the firm said, although SpaceX has deep pockets. In a LinkedIn post from last week, T-Mobile’s CTO said, “You can acquire spectrum in a single transaction. You cannot acquire a nationwide, high-performing wireless network overnight.” He put Starlink Mobile’s holdings at 80 megahertz after the proposed acquisition, some of it uplink-only, compared with T-Mobile’s nearly 400 megahertz of low-band and mid-band spectrum. Building that network, he said, takes years of investment and construction. Wireless networks are built “site by site, neighborhood by neighborhood,” he wrote, including coverage inside buildings and other hard-to-reach places. Stifel reaffirmed its 'Buy' rating and $190 price target on SpaceX, implying a 17% upside from current levels. The firm called the spectrum acquisition “a new investment in SPCX’s mobile business” and said it advances SpaceX’s wireless plans alongside approval for up to 15,000 next-generation Starlink Mobile satellites. Stifel outlined three possible paths for SpaceX: build a terrestrial network, partner with existing operators or develop a different architecture. This whole 800mhz spectrum dream, which isn't even going to slightly begin until next year, news has faded.” Another user said, “$GSAT $AAPL Should just cut a deal with $SPCX already and BUY Globalstar” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Telecom analyst Roger Entner said SpaceX could build a "massive" midband spectrum position if it secured additional spectrum associated with Ligado and Viasat and won licenses in a proposed FCC auction. This brings AST SpaceMobile's spectrum strategy under fresh scrutiny. ASTS stock rose nearly 1% to $51.46 on Monday, recovering slightly after a 16% slide over the previous two sessions. The selloff followed SpaceX’s agreement last week to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800-megahertz spectrum portfolio, putting the satellite-to-phone spectrum race back in focus. Entner said major carriers are likely to contest the 25 megahertz of spectrum the FCC has proposed auctioning. “Every major carrier will likely bid on these licenses for either offensive or defensive reasons,” he said. His bigger scenario is based on Ligado and Viasat. “If Elon Musk acquires Ligado and Viasat and secures this new spectrum, Starlink could control a massive midband block for terrestrial and direct to device services,” Entner said. On the other hand, ARK Investment Management analyst Tasha Keeney sees SpaceX’s recent spectrum deal and satellite authorization as building blocks for a broader mobile push. “Together, the two moves give Starlink Mobile a credible path to becoming a full mobile carrier instead of a dead-zone backup,” she said. Keeney said low-band spectrum could improve indoor coverage, while ground radios and small cellular units linked to Starlink dish infrastructure could add capacity where needed. The FCC is seeking comment on auctioning spectrum in the 1675–1695 MHz and 2020-2025 MHz bands. Its proposal would allow flexible use for terrestrial wireless, direct-to-device service or both. Final rules and an auction date have not been set. The bands sit next to the spectrum associated with AWS-4, Ligado and Viasat. SpaceX already has a major satellite step in place: The FCC authorized it to deploy up to 15,000 next-generation satellites for direct-to-device service. SpaceX says the system will work with spectrum around 2 GHz and deliver substantially more bandwidth than its current generation. SpaceX has agreed to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800 MHz portfolio, including up to 14 MHz of paired low-band spectrum. The deal still needs FCC approval. Neither company disclosed the price, though reports have put it at $8 billion. The low-band frequencies can travel farther and penetrate buildings better than higher-frequency signals, helping address a weakness of satellite-to-phone service. SpaceX’s plans also call for ground-based radios on towers, rooftops and other structures. Keeney has pointed to small cellular units connected to Starlink dish infrastructure as another way to add capacity, while noting that dish locations may not line up with areas of high mobile demand. AST’s own spectrum plans hinge on a conditional arrangement with Ligado. Under a 2025 term sheet, AST would receive long-term rights to use up to 40 MHz of Ligado’s L-band spectrum in the U.S. and Canada, plus access to 5 MHz in the 1670-1675 MHz band. The segment borders the lower edge of the FCC’s proposed 1675–1695 MHz auction band. While AST SpaceMobile relies on carrier partnerships to connect its satellites with ordinary phones, SpaceX is assembling a more direct mobile-network model that combines satellites, spectrum and ground infrastructure. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for ASTS slipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 338% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One bearish user said, “$ASTS trending for no reason. No commercial revenue. No profits. Launches promised like they promised they would not do another offering (they did and never apologized or explained themselves). You cant trust them.” Another user said, “$ASTS classic pump and dump. Not sure how they get away with it. Wonder how many longs wish they sold in the 80's....” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) stock gained overnight after the company unveiled a 24-kilowatt (kW) power delivery board developed with Nvidia (NVDA) to improve AI data center efficiency. Navitas targets 97% efficiency with the system, reduced power losses, and greater space savings. Navitas Semiconductor stock traded over 1% higher overnight, ahead of Tuesday. The stock fell 7% to its worst day in over a month in the regular session. Developed with Nvidia, Navitas’ 24-kilowatt board eliminates an intermediate conversion stage that traditionally changes 50 volts to 12 volts. By removing this step, the system aims to cut energy losses, simplify power distribution, and free up space on circuit boards The product expands Navitas' portfolio of high-voltage power solutions for AI infrastructure. It follows a previously announced 20 kW system that converts 800 volts to 6 volts, also developed along with Nvidia. Navitas expects the new board to achieve 97% efficiency at full power, with power density exceeding 2,000 watts per cubic inch. Its design follows a 400-by-60-millimeter format developed for Nvidia's latest systems, allowing installation on the compute motherboard near the processors. Placing power conversion closer to graphics processing units and other compute processors can help limit electricity losses as power travels through a system. The board is designed to supply an entire compute tray, addressing the substantial energy requirements of advanced AI computing equipment. The system uses 16 gallium nitride (GaN) transistors at 650 volts. Navitas’ GaNFast technology and dual-cooling design help convert power efficiently while keeping the system compact. “The next era of AI will be defined not only by how much compute we can create, but by our ability to deliver the power needed to unleash its full potential,” said Chris Allexandre, President and CEO, Navitas. A spike in the bond yields of CoreWeave, a cloud provider that rents out AI computing power, revived worries about debt-heavy AI customers and dragged semiconductor shares lower, according to Yahoo Finance. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), both an investor in CoreWeave and its chip supplier, slipped with the group. Nvidia designs the processors and networking gear that train and run AI models, and sells them as complete data center systems to cloud giants, AI labs, and specialists like CoreWeave. Gamers know it for its graphics cards, but data centers now bring in the vast majority of its revenue. So the selloff raised a sharp question: is Nvidia's growth only as sturdy as the balance sheets of the companies buying its chips? The answer depends less on one cloud provider than on who else is paying. Whatever its customers are doing, Nvidia itself is enormously profitable. Over the past 12 months, it earned $192.88 billion in net income and kept about 65% of its sales as operating profit. Those margins come from pricing power: buyers pay up because Nvidia sells the chips, the networking, and the software developers already build on. That edge has compounded for years, with revenue growing about 66.9% a year over the past five years. AI spending has been the common thread for the wider chip group covered in 12 Best Performing Semiconductor Stocks to Invest In. The latest results show the moat widening. In its fiscal second quarter of 2027, revenue reached $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year earlier, and data center revenue rose 117% to $89.0 billion. Management guided third-quarter revenue to $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, without counting on any data center compute sales in China. The customer list argues against a single point of failure. The new Vera Rubin platform is in full production at partners including Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle, not just CoreWeave, and CEO Jensen Huang said in the release that a broader base of AI labs and startups is scaling at the same time. Nvidia is also lining up outside money: financing platforms with firms including Apollo, BlackRock, and KKR aim to mobilize more than $500 billion in third-party capital, subject to final agreements. The buildout behind those orders runs well beyond chips, into the names in 15 Best Data Center Stocks to Buy and Hold for the Next Decade. That financing push cuts both ways, and it's the heart of the bear case. Specialist providers like CoreWeave are building AI capacity with borrowed money, and Nvidia sits on both sides of some of those deals, as supplier and investor. This week, CoreWeave's debt load and the prospect of higher interest rates were enough to shake the whole chip group, according to Yahoo Finance. Huang pushed back at a Bloomberg event in Stockholm, saying CoreWeave's position is strengthening and its cost of capital is falling, according to Yahoo Finance. Still, a credit squeeze would hit the most leveraged buyers first, and it would show up as softer orders long before it touched Nvidia's margins. For now, the guidance points the other way. The market has marked the stock down for exactly this risk. Nvidia trades at about 23 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, roughly 45% below its five-year average of about 42 times, and only modestly above the technology sector's median of about 21 times. That small premium is the striking part, given that analysts' consensus expects earnings per share to grow about 95% this fiscal year. The five-year average was set when investors paid ahead for growth that hadn't arrived; now the earnings have arrived, and the multiple has fallen to meet them. Investors hunting for AI exposure at a lower price have a wider set to weigh in 10 Undervalued AI Stocks to Buy Now. The multiple rests on adjusted earnings, which came in below GAAP earnings last quarter, so it isn't flattering the picture. What the price does assume is that growth slows sharply after this year, or that the financing chain behind AI spending breaks. The evidence points to a valuation reflecting financing fears more than any crack in the business. For investors who can sit through sharp swings in chip stocks and are looking several years out, the setup looks stronger than the selloff suggests. A guidance cut tied to customers pulling back on borrowed spending, or financing platforms that fail to reach final agreements, would change that picture quickly. content: Cathie Wood-led Ark Invest's portfolios saw some dramatic winners and losers in the third quarter (Q3), with artificial intelligence, biotech, crypto and other disruptive-technology bets among the biggest drivers. Ark's latest quarterly report shows that several stocks made meaningful contributions across multiple ETFs, while Tesla Inc. (TSLA) and Rocket Lab Corp. (RKLB) emerged among the most notable drags. Ark's attribution figures measure each holding's contribution to its ETF's performance, rather than the stock's standalone return. 10x Genomics Inc. (TXG) was the standout winner across Ark's portfolios. The stock contributed 9.03 percentage points to ARK Genomic Revolution ETF’s (ARKG) 28.92% Q3 gain and 2.92 points to ARK Innovation ETF’s (ARKK) 10.39% return during the quarter. Ark attributed the rally to growing interest in single-cell sequencing and spatial analysis as sources of data for AI drug-discovery models. The firm also highlighted the launch of 10x's Atera spatial system, with orders already in place for the 40 shipments anticipated in 2026. Twist Bioscience Corp. (TWST) was another major biotech winner, contributing 6.51 points to ARKG and 2.55 points to ARKK. The stock jumped 87.83% during the quarter. Ark said Twist was increasingly recognized as a beneficiary of AI-driven drug discovery, including through its protein-characterization work for Anthropic. Tempus AI Inc. (TEM) also stood out, contributing 3.21 points to ARKG and 2.08 points to ARKK, while gaining 41.38% during the quarter. Then there was Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR), emerging as one of the most important cross-ETF winners. Palantir contributed 1.86 points to ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ), 1.62 points to ARKK, 1.48 points to ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW), 2.39 points to ARK Blockchain & Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF) and 1.47 points to ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX). Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) also made the cut, particularly across Ark's technology-focused portfolios. It contributed 0.49 points to ARKQ and 0.48 points to ARKX. Tesla was the clearest recurring drag across Ark's portfolios. It was the biggest detractor in ARKQ (-1.72 percentage points), ARKK (-1.75 points) and ARKW (-1.43 points). Ark said Tesla sold off sharply after its second-quarter (Q2) results disappointed on profitability, with price cuts and the wind-down of the Model S and Model X pressuring margins. But the firm also pointed to a recovery in the stock as Tesla publicly launched Cybercab in Austin and surpassed 1 million unsupervised robotaxi miles, up from 380,000 just six weeks earlier. Rocket Lab was another major drag, particularly in the space-focused portfolios. It contributed -1.39 points to ARKQ and -2.04 points to ARKX. The firm noted that Rocket Lab completed 21 flights in 2025 and had a backlog of more than 90 missions as of the second quarter. Ark's biggest winners included AI, AI-enabled biotech and other technology bets, while some of its highest-profile holdings, most notably Tesla and Rocket Lab, weighed on performance. Should retail investors view this as a buying opportunity? Nvidia isn't the only AI chipmaker around, but its chips are critical providers of power for the high-level inference and reasoning that support AI functions. That means all large models require Nvidia chips and, increasingly, full Nvidia compute systems. It recently launched its latest platform, Vera Rubin, which combines Rubin graphics processing units (GPUs), Vera central processing units (CPUs), large quantities of high bandwidth memory, and other hardware to deliver high processing power. The company's revenue growth has recently accelerated, with the top line more than doubling year over year in its fiscal 2027 second quarter (which ended July 26). Management already provided fiscal 2028 guidance for 70% growth, which would be a serious feat given how large the company already is. That 4% drop doesn't on its own create an incredible buying opportunity. However, it might be a good time to buy the stock if you've been planning to anyway. The more pressing concern is what the market is actually worried about: whether OpenAI's news is actually bad news for Nvidia. There's some risk there that investors should keep in mind. Nvidia stock is well-priced right now, trading at less than 14 times forward one-year earnings. I wouldn't make it the central component of your portfolio, but Nvidia looks like a buy right now. title: Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA Expand Strategic Partnership to Advance Safe Highly Automated Driving in the Next Decade - NVIDIA Newsroom

Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA today announced that they will extend their strategic partnership to advance the next generation of automated driving systems. The collaboration brings together Mercedes-Benz’s automotive engineering and safety expertise and its MB.OS operating system with NVIDIA’s accelerated computing and AI technologies. “NVIDIA is our most important strategic partner in automated driving. Together, we developed the first Mercedes-Benz assistance system for urban point-to-point driving for the western world,” Jörg Burzer, member of the board of management of Mercedes‑Benz Group AG and chief technology officer, development and procurement. “The expansion of our partnership marks a significant milestone and reflects the mutual trust we have built over the years. Together, we aim to bring further pioneering innovations to the road, offering our customers the best automated driving experience while upholding the high safety standards they expect from a Mercedes-Benz.” “Accelerated computing is giving vehicles the intelligence to understand the world and reason through complex driving situations,” said Ali Kani, vice president of automotive at NVIDIA. “Mercedes-Benz brings the engineering excellence and commitment to safety this transformation demands. Together, we’re building on NVIDIA Hyperion to bring that intelligence and full-stack safety to the road and make autonomous driving an everyday reality.” Mercedes-Benz’s MB.OS operating system supports new driving functions and over-the-air updates, working with NVIDIA Hyperion’s in-vehicle computing and sensor architecture. NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack provides full-stack driving software with AI reasoning capabilities, supporting point-to-point urban assistance, active safety and automated parking. NVIDIA Halos adds to the Mercedes-Benz safety foundation, including a parallel safety stack that adds redundancy and guardrails. Together, these technologies support advanced driver assistance and the development of future SAE-Level 4 applications, including robolimousines. Beyond automated driving, Mercedes-Benz also relies on NVIDIA technologies for vehicle engineering simulation and within MO360, its digital production ecosystem — from virtual planning to AI-based applications.
